module_title: Doha Round, Dispute Settlement, and India's 'Peace Clause'
introduction: This advanced level explores the geopolitical battleground of the WTO, focusing on the conflict between rich and poor nations over food security and the paralysis of its judicial system.

core_concepts.title: Dispute Settlement Body (DSB)
core_concepts.description: This is the 'Supreme Court' of the WTO. If a country (e.g., the USA) believes another country (e.g., India) is violating a trade agreement, it files a case with the DSB. The DSB's rulings are legally binding, and it can authorize trade sanctions against the guilty country.

core_concepts.title: Doha Development Round (Launched in 2001)
core_concepts.description: This is the current, ongoing round of WTO trade negotiations. Its primary objective was to improve the trading prospects of 'Developing Countries' (by forcing rich countries to stop heavily subsidizing their rich farmers). Due to severe disagreements between developed and developing nations, the Doha Round has been 'deadlocked' for over two decades.

core_concepts.title: The Bali Package and 'Peace Clause' (2013)
core_concepts.description: India heavily subsidizes its farmers via MSP (Minimum Support Price) and provides cheap grain to the poor via the PDS. This violates the WTO's 'Amber Box' limit (which is capped at 10% of total agricultural production). At the 2013 Bali Ministerial Conference, India successfully negotiated a 'Peace Clause' to protect its food security program.

core_concepts.title: What does the Peace Clause mean?
core_concepts.description: It provides a legal shield. It means that no WTO member country can drag India to the Dispute Settlement Body for breaching the 10% subsidy limit on staple crops, until a 'permanent solution' regarding public stockholding for food security is found.

important_entities.name: Appellate Body Crisis
important_entities.significance: In recent years, the United States has deliberately blocked the appointment of new judges to the WTO's Appellate Body (the highest appeals court). Because it lacks a quorum of judges, the WTO's entire dispute settlement mechanism is currently 'paralyzed'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: This is the maximum limit of Amber Box subsidies a country can give. For developing countries (like India), it is '10%' of the total value of agricultural production. For developed countries (like the USA), it is stricter at '5%'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The 'Peace Clause' was signed at the Bali Ministerial Conference in 2013.

exam_strategy_tips: For UPSC Mains, 'Is the WTO losing its relevance?' and 'The Failure of the Doha Round' are top-tier essay and analysis topics. Always mention the Appellate Body crisis as proof of its decline.
